'''Alan David Sokal''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|s|oʊ|k|əl}} {{respell|SOH|kəl}}; born January 24, 1955) is an American professor of [[mathematics]] at [[University College London]] and professor emeritus of [[physics]] at [[New York University]]. He works with [[statistical mechanics]] and [[combinatorics]].

Sokal is a critic of [[postmodernism]], and caused the [[Sokal affair]] in 1996 when his deliberately nonsensical paper was published by [[Duke University Press]]'s ''[[Social Text]]''. He also co-authored a paper criticizing the [[critical positivity ratio]] concept in [[positive psychology]].

==Early life and academic career==
Sokal was born to [[Nathan O. Sokal]] (1929–2016), an electrical engineer of Polish descent, and Zelda Kaufman Sokal.<ref name="microwave">{{cite journal |last1=Raab |first1=Frederick H. |title=Recollections of Nathan Sokal: The Man, His Work, and the Class-E Amplifier |journal=IEEE Microwave Magazine |date=2018 |volume=19 |issue=5 |doi=10.1109/MMM.2018.2823240}}</ref> He received his [[Bachelor of Arts]] degree from [[Harvard College]] in 1976 and his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] from [[Princeton University]] in 1981.<ref name="mtt">{{cite web |title=Alan Sokal |url=https://mtt.org/profile/alan-sokal/ |website=mtt.org |access-date=December 28, 2025}}</ref> He was advised by the physicist [[Arthur Wightman]]. During the summers of 1986, 1987, and 1988, Sokal taught [[mathematics]] at the [[National Autonomous University of Nicaragua]], when the [[Sandinistas]] controlled the elected government.

==Research interests==
Sokal's research involves [[mathematical physics]] and combinatorics. In particular, he studies the interplay between these topics based on questions concerning statistical mechanics and [[quantum field theory]]. This includes work on the [[chromatic polynomial]] and the [[Tutte polynomial]], which appear both in [[algebraic graph theory]] and in the study of [[phase transition]]s in statistical mechanics. His interests include [[computational physics]] and [[algorithms]], such as [[Markov chain Monte Carlo]] algorithms for problems in statistical physics. He also co-authored a book on [[quantum triviality]].<ref>{{cite book|last1=Fernandez |first1=R. |last2=Froehlich |first2=J. |author-link2=Juerg Froehlich |last3=Sokal |first3=A. D. |date=1992 |title=Random Walks, Critical Phenomena, and Triviality in Quantum Field Theory |publisher=Springer |isbn=0-387-54358-9}}</ref>

In 2013, Sokal co-authored a paper with Nicholas Brown and Harris Friedman, rejecting the [[Losada Line]], a concept popular in [[positive psychology]]. Named after its proposer, [[Marcial Losada]], it refers to a critical range for an individual's ratio of positive to [[negative emotion]]s, outside of which the individual will tend to have poorer life and occupational outcomes.<ref>{{cite journal |author=Losada M |year=1999 |title=The complex dynamics of high performance teams |url=http://losada.socialpsychology.org |journal=Mathematical and Computer Modelling |volume=30 |issue=9–10 |pages=179–192 |doi=10.1016/s0895-7177(99)00189-2 |doi-access=|url-access=subscription }}</ref> This concept of a critical positivity ratio was much cited and popularised by psychologists such as [[Barbara Fredrickson]]. The trio's paper, published in ''American Psychologist'', contended that the ratio was based on faulty mathematical reasoning and therefore invalid.<ref>{{cite journal |last1= Brown |first1=N. J. L. |last2=Sokal |first2=A. D. |last3= Friedman |first3=H. L. |year=2013 |title=The Complex Dynamics of Wishful Thinking: The Critical Positivity Ratio |journal=American Psychologist |volume=68 |issue=9 |pages=801–813 |pmid=23855896 |doi=10.1037/a0032850 |arxiv=1307.7006 |s2cid=644769 }}</ref>

During his high school years and undergraduate studies at Harvard in the 1970s, Sokal collaborated with his father, Nathan, on his work on [[RF power amplifier]]s:<ref name="microwave"/> their work was motivated by their mutual interest in [[amateur radio]].<ref name="class-e">{{cite journal |last1=Sokal |first1=Nathan O. |title=The Origin and Development of the High Efficiency Class-E RF Power Amplifier: A 2011 Address Accepting the Honorary Doctorate |journal=IEEE Microwave Magazine |date=2018 |volume=19 |issue=5 |pages=22-25 |doi=10.1109/MMM.2018.2823241}}</ref> This has resulted in the introduction of [[Power amplifier classes#Class_E|class-E]] high-efficiency power amplifier,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Sokal |first1=N. O |last2=Sokal |first2=A. D. |title=Class E-A new class of high-efficiency tuned single-ended switching power amplifiers |journal=[[IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits]] |date=1975 |volume=10 |issue=3 |pages=168-176 |doi=10.1109/JSSC.1975.1050582}}</ref> and Sokals were awarded the U.S. Patents 3,900,823 and 3,919,656. In 2007, Alan and Nathan Sokal were awarded Microwave Pioneer Award by [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers|IEEE]] Microwave Theory and Technology Society for "development of the class E power amplifier."<ref name="mtt"/><ref name="mtt-2007">{{cite web |title=2007 Microwave Pioneer Award |url=https://mtt.org/app/uploads/2019/01/2007_A_Sokal.pdf |website=mtt.org |access-date=December 28, 2025}}</ref>

== Critiques of postmodernism ==

=== Sokal affair ===
{{Main|Sokal affair}}

In 1996, Sokal was curious whether the then-non-peer-reviewed [[Postmodern philosophy|postmodern]] [[cultural studies]] journal ''Social Text'' (published by [[Duke University Press]]) would publish a submission which "flattered the editors' ideological preconceptions". Sokal submitted a grand-sounding but completely nonsensical paper titled "Transgressing the Boundaries: Toward a Transformative [[Hermeneutics]] of Quantum Gravity".<ref>{{cite journal |last= Sokal |first=A. |title=Transgressing the Boundaries: Toward a Transformative Hermeneutics of Quantum Gravity |year=1996 |journal=Social Text |volume=46/47 |pages=217–252 |doi=10.2307/466856 |issue=46/47 |jstor=466856}}</ref><ref>[http://www.physics.nyu.edu/faculty/sokal/transgress_v2/transgress_v2_singlefile.html Transgressing the Boundaries: Toward a Transformative Hermeneutics of Quantum Gravity]</ref>

After holding the article back from earlier issues because of Sokal's refusal to consider revisions, the staff published it in the "Science Wars" issue as a relevant contribution.<ref>Robbins, Bruce and Ross, Andrew. http://physics.nyu.edu/sokal/SocialText_reply_LF.pdf Editorial Response to the hoax, explaining Social Text's decision to publish</ref> Soon thereafter, Sokal then revealed that the article was a [[hoax]] in the journal ''[[Lingua Franca (magazine)|Lingua Franca]]'',<ref>{{cite journal |last=Sokal |first=A. |year=1996 |title=A Physicist Experiments with Cultural Studies |journal=Lingua Franca |pages=62–64 |url=http://www.physics.nyu.edu/faculty/sokal/lingua_franca_v4.pdf }}</ref> arguing that [[Left-wing politics|leftists]] and [[social science]] would be better served by intellectual underpinnings based on [[reason]]. The affair was front-page news in ''[[The New York Times]]'' on May 18, 1996.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Scott |first=Janny |date=1996-05-18 |title=Postmodern Gravity Deconstructed, Slyly |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1996/05/18/nyregion/postmodern-gravity-deconstructed-slyly.html |access-date=2026-08-17 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> Sokal responded to leftist and postmodernist criticism of the deception by asserting that he was himself a leftist, and that his motivation was to "defend the Left from a trendy segment of itself".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sokal's Reply to Social Text Editorial |url=https://physics.nyu.edu/sokal/reply.html |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=physics.nyu.edu}}</ref>

Sokal followed up in 1997 by co-authoring the book ''[[Fashionable Nonsense|Impostures Intellectuelles]]'' with physicist and philosopher of science [[Jean Bricmont]]  (published in English, a year later, as ''Fashionable Nonsense''). The book accuses some social sciences academics of using scientific and mathematical terms incorrectly and criticizes proponents of the "[[strong program]]" of the [[Sociology of scientific knowledge|sociology of science]] for denying the value of truth. The book had contrasted reviews, with some lauding the effort,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Dawkins |first=Richard |title=Postmodernism disrobed |journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]] |volume=394 |issue=6689 |date=July 1998 |pages=141–143 |doi=10.1038/28089 |doi-access=free |url=http://www.physics.nyu.edu/sokal/dawkins.html |bibcode=1998Natur.394..141D |s2cid=40887987 |url-access=subscription }}</ref> and some more reserved.<ref>
{{Cite journal |last=Hilgartner |first=Stephen |date=Autumn 1997 |title=The Sokal Affair in Context |journal=Science, Technology, & Human Values |volume=22 | issue=4 |pages=506–522 |doi=10.1177/016224399702200404 |s2cid=145740247 }}</ref><ref>
{{Cite journal |last=Epstein |first=William M. |title=Confirmational response bias among social work journals |journal=[[Science, Technology, & Human Values]] |volume=15 |issue=1 |year=1990 |pages = 9–38 |doi=10.1177/016224399001500102 |s2cid=140863997 }}</ref>

In 2008, Sokal reviewed the Sokal affair and its implications in the book ''[[Beyond the Hoax]]''.

=== Other critiques ===
In 2024, Sokal co-authored an opinion-editorial article in the newspaper ''[[The Boston Globe]]'' with evolutionary biologist [[Richard Dawkins]] criticizing the use of the terminology "sex assigned at birth" instead of "sex" by the [[American Medical Association]], the [[American Psychological Association]], the [[American Academy of Pediatrics]], and the [[Centers for Disease Control and Prevention]]. Sokal and Dawkins argued that [[Biological sex|sex]] is an "objective biological reality" that "is determined at conception and is then ''observed'' at birth", rather than [[Sex assignment|assigned]] by a medical professional. Terming this "[[social constructionism]] gone amok", Sokal and Dawkins argued further that "distort[ing] the scientific facts in the service of a social cause" risks undermining trust in medical institutions.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Sokal |first1=Alan |last2=Dawkins |first2=Richard |date=April 8, 2024 |title=Sex and gender: The medical establishment's reluctance to speak honestly about biological reality |url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/2024/04/08/opinion/sex-gender-medical-terms/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240408223633/https://www.bostonglobe.com/2024/04/08/opinion/sex-gender-medical-terms/ |archive-date=April 8, 2024 |access-date=April 8, 2024 |work=[[The Boston Globe]]}}</ref> Sokal repeated these criticisms in an editorial for the magazine [[The Critic (modern magazine)|''The Critic'']] discussing the more general [[politicization of science]], especially biology and medicine.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Sokal |first=Alan |date=May 14, 2024 |title=Woke invades the sciences |url=https://thecritic.co.uk/woke-invades-the-sciences/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20240524171147/https://thecritic.co.uk/woke-invades-the-sciences/ |archive-date=May 24, 2024 |access-date=May 26, 2024 |work=[[The Critic (modern magazine)|The Critic]]}}</ref>
